title: The Man, in Life Wherever Placed
description: The Man, in Life Wherever Placed in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Robert Burns wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 413 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Happiness of the Righteous”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The man, in life wher-ev-er placed, Hath happ-i-ness in store, Who walks not in the wic-ked's way, Nor learns their guilt-y lore:

lines: The man, in life wherever placed,
Who walks not in the wicked's way,
Nor from the seat of scornful pride
That man shall flourish like the trees
The fruitful top is spread on high,
But he whose blossom buds in guilt
Shall to the ground be cast,
And, like the rootless stubble, tossed

licence: Public domain: Robert Burns died in 1796.
credits: Words by Robert Burns (1759–1796), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
